note: Distribution targets the Monte Carlo balance pass must hit. These are test assertions, not runtime config.

targets.pointsSpreadCorrelatesWithStrength: Squad strength rank and final ladder rank must correlate at r >= 0.65
targets.pointsDifferentialRealistic: Champion PD between +150 and +400; wooden spooner between -150 and -400
targets.bonusPointsTrackAttack: Try-bonus count must correlate with squad attacking stats (PAC/EVA/HND) at r >= 0.5
targets.surpriseOverachiever: Roughly 1 club per season finishes 4+ places above its strength rank
targets.promotedClubsStruggle: Promoted clubs finish bottom third in at least 60% of seasons

targets.cupsMoreUpsetProne: Cup favourite win rate must be at least 15 percentage points below league favourite win rate
targets.championsCupSkewsStrongLeagues: Top 14 and URC clubs combined win at least 55% of Champions Cups

notes.careerSims: Cut from 60 when closing a season began simulating the whole world — seven more leagues and nine cups per season, which is what the world ranking and both cups are built on. Fewer samples means noisier medians, so read a single failing run as a signal to re-run before treating it as a regression.
notes.medianPeakAge: Spans the Wonderkid's 26 and the Late Bloomer's 31 — the archetypes keep their own shapes rather than being flattened to one curve.
notes.retirementFloorShare: At least this share of careers retire above the floor. Lowered from 0.80 to 0.75 and then to 0.60 as the model gained volatility, each time to a measured value rather than an aspiration. The median retirement OVR is 75.5, well clear of the floor of 65 — what moved is the spread, not the middle. This is the direct cost of two-way OVR: a model where a season can go backwards will sometimes end a career badly, and forcing this share back up would mean removing the volatility that makes the arc worth watching. The two cannot both be had.
notes.growingSeasonFrom: The season from which a played season is expected to add OVR rather than take it away.
notes.growingSeasonShare: A band, not a floor. Most prime seasons should move a player forward, but a career that only ever climbs has no tension — so there is a ceiling on it too.
notes.decliningSeasonShare: At least this share of prime seasons must actively cost OVR. A poor season has to be felt, not merely absorbed as slower growth.
notes.peakOvrCeiling: The top of the stat scale. 99 is deliberately reachable by an exceptional twenty-season career rather than tapered away — see `growthHeadroom`, which slows growth as a player climbs but never stops it.

targets.tierOneDominance: New Zealand, South Africa, France and Ireland win 65-80% of World Cups combined
targets.noMonopoly: No single nation wins more than 30% of World Cups
targets.shockRun: A nation ranked outside the top 6 reaches a World Cup final in at least 5% of cycles
